1 used to go to school when the applicant used to misbehaved with her.

In the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated that the applicant used to misbehaved with her,
however, in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., for the first time, she stated that wrong was also committed on her on 10.06.2024.
In the medical report, which was done on 21.06.2024, there was no corroboration of allegation of rape.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the huge variance in both the statements of the victim coupled with the fact that the medical does not corroborate the allegation levelled against the applicant coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since24.06.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Lavkush be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
